extracted.intended_audience: national and local governments, representatives of civil society organizations, OGP members and partners, and others designing public participation reforms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for governments and civil society on embedding fit‑for‑purpose, high‑quality, and inclusive public participation across sectors, processes, and institutions — including legal, institutional, capacity‑building, and pilot reforms. Intended to inform action plans and commitments under the Open Gov Challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge prompt: mainstream fit-for-purpose participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mainstream or embed fit-for-purpose, high quality and inclusive public participation practices across key government sectors, processes, and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching objective for reforms and commitments under the Open Gov Challenge (2023–2028). Actions should be adapted to domestic context and coordinated across levels and branches of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass and implement laws and policies to enable participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Passing and implementing laws and policies that create the expectation and/or possibility of a higher level of public participation across the policy-making process (e.g. establishing legally enforceable participation requirements or new mechanisms for participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include legally enforceable participation requirements; these are tagged as Foundational reforms. Use legislation and policy to create predictable opportunities for public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish legal right to participation and access to information (notice-and-comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a legal right to participation and access to information through common mechanisms, such as notice-and-comment periods in regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically names notice-and-comment as a common mechanism; links participation rights with access to information so the public can meaningfully engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve access to decision-making processes (open meetings, RTI, lobbying rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish that the public has a right to observe and inform public decisions through open meeting laws, right to information, and lobbying rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open meeting laws, right-to-information regimes, and lobbying rules to create public-facing opportunities to observe and influence decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop minimum standards on deliberative practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop government standards that govern participation practice, either to elaborate on existing laws or to provide guidance for innovations in deliberative processes already being implemented by administrations or legislatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards can formalize good practices for deliberation and participation methods; this is classified as Intermediate difficulty and typically sits in the executive branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create oversight bodies (multi-stakeholder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish multi-stakeholder bodies at the agency or whole-of-government level that design, mainstream, and monitor inclusion and participation practices in agency decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bodies may be housed in legislative oversight committees; they should be diverse, inclusive, and appointed using transparent, well-publicized processes. Tagged Intermediate difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create participation teams / institutional knowledge teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish participation teams or centers of best practice to maintain institutional knowledge and increase the quality of participation mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These teams institutionalize capacity, collect lessons learned, and support replication of successful practices. Tagged Advanced difficulty when institutionalizing at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design pilots of deliberative processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out pilots of deliberative processes on key issues with the general public, paying special attention to ensure diversity across and within groups of the selected sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilots (e.g., citizen assemblies) are often effective at the local level; use pilots to test methods and build evidence before scaling. Tagged Foundational for some uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish rules for interaction between deliberative processes and policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly explain how deliberative processes will interact with constitutional, legislative, and regulatory processes, such as clarifying when they will occur and how they will inform final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set procedures for deliberative polling, assemblies, and how outputs feed into formal decision points so participants and the public understand impact and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct targeted outreach to identify new actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct targeted outreach for new actors who will join participation initiatives to ensure that groups are as inclusive and representative as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach should proactively recruit underrepresented groups and build representative samples for deliberation. Tagged Intermediate difficulty and often implemented by executive/legislative actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure diversity and representativeness in participant selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay special attention to ensure diversity across and within groups of the selected sample (to increase inclusivity and representativeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection methods should aim for demographic and experiential diversity, especially when piloting deliberative processes; examples and research indicate better outcomes when diversity is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train public officials on public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out training and capacity building for public officials on public participation to ensure that high-quality, meaningful dialogue takes place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training equips officials to design and facilitate participation processes and to respond to public input effectively. Tagged Intermediate difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train members of the public who join participation initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out training and capacity building for members of the public who join participation initiatives, especially representatives from groups not likely to be involved in decision-making (e.g., young people, indigenous people, women).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building participants' capacity ensures meaningful participation and helps equalize power dynamics within deliberative settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transparency measures (publish information, open data standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency activities include proactive or reactive publication of government-held information, legal/institutional frameworks to strengthen the right to access information, and disclosing information using open data standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency empowers citizens to exercise rights and participate; use open data and accessible disclosures to support informed engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design civic participation mechanisms (new/improved processes; include underrepresented groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create new or improved processes and mechanisms for the public to contribute to decisions, including participatory mechanisms to involve underrepresented groups in policy making and a legal environment that guarantees civil and political rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms range from consultations to deliberative assemblies; design choices should prioritize inclusion and legal protections for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen public accountability mechanisms (citizen audits, appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public accountability means institutions must justify actions, act upon requirements and criticisms, and provide mechanisms that the public can access to trigger accountability (e.g., citizen audits, citizen-initiated appeals processes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure participation links to accountability pathways so inputs can influence outcomes and institutions can be held to commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize inclusion (increase voice of historically discriminated groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion is fundamental: increase the voice, agency, and influence of historically discriminated or underrepresented groups, who may face discrimination based on gender, sexual identity, race, ethnicity, age, geography, differing ability, legal, or socioeconomic status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outreach, selection, facilitation, and support (e.g., training, accessibility) to remove barriers to participation for these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag reforms by Degree of Difficulty (Foundational / Intermediate / Advanced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforms are categorized as Foundational (essential building blocks), Intermediate (complex, requiring coordination), or Advanced (ambitious, closing loopholes or institutionalizing practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tags to sequence reforms and set realistic timelines; foundational reforms often establish legal frameworks, while advanced actions institutionalize proven practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage digital platforms and tools for co-creation and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop or use online platforms for policy co-creation where the public can access edit history, meeting records, and reasoned government responses to feedback related to policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include centralized platforms for legislative co-creation and public engagement platforms that increase accessibility and traceability of inputs and government responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide examples and models (frameworks, consultation models, engagement tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt or adapt frameworks, consultation models, and tools (e.g., participation frameworks, dialogue models, community engagement tools) used by other governments and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists country examples (e.g., participation frameworks, platforms, consultative models) and external resources (OECD, Council of Europe, Involve, People Powered) to guide implementation and design choices.
